title: DCLab's long agents behind the chat: the understanding and solution teams end to end, notebook cells, the solution save, and long writes (agents plan steps 2, 3 and 5)
request: The owner (2026-10-26): every agentic system already built in R&D behind DCLab Code's chat, used and adopted, not rebuilt (plan ~/.claude/plans/joyful-jingling-engelbart.md; $20 budget).
spec: the agents plan, steps 2 (the long agents), 3 (data and notebook agents) and 5 (sync-check locks the person's routes)
plan: live-check each long agent through DCLab Code with DCLab's model on, capped
fix what each run finds, failing test first, in the repository that owns the cause
sync-check finds every route DCLab Code relays, sends or reads in R&D, and locks R&D's list of the person's writes
a row per R&D agent in PARITY_PLAN: reached, tested, live-checked, or why it stays the person's

decisions.decision: Accepting the agent's notebook cell is relayed only with the cell's whole code on the card, read from DCLab first
decisions.why: a person's yes to code they never saw is no decision; a cell that cannot be shown whole is answered on DCLab's page

decisions.decision: The solution save (PUT) is relayed with a larger body limit (6,000 characters), still shown whole
decisions.why: a solution names every column kept out with its reason; refusing it would leave team-built projects stuck in the chat

decisions.decision: A long write goes on in R&D and the chat is told how to follow it, instead of raising the SDK's limit alone
decisions.why: a team walk can take longer than any fixed limit; cutting it halfway would leave half-done work, and a timeout invites a second send

decisions.decision: The twin, the research campaign, Kaggle and the store's runs stay outside the chat
decisions.why: the owner's switch, the owner's Claude-only rule (the campaign needs OpenAI), the owner's key, and the owner's make targets

change: dclab-code: config.js (notebook answer and solution save relayed; holdout patterns narrowed; ownGuards; copied defaults; PERSON_READS), engine.js (cellShown), guards.js (whenBody), dclab.js (300 s tool limit; writeOperations, readsListed), dclab_person.js (reads with the person's token), rd.js and scripts/sync-check.js (personRouteChanges, personWrites), docs/PARITY_PLAN.md (a row per R&D agent). R&D: chat_agents.py (the understanding team a chat write; long writes go on), orchestra/solution.py (the report), route docstrings naming body fields.

findings.defect: a cell the agent wrote could not be accepted from the chat
findings.scenario: s_b13975a1cb49: notebook/write relayed, the run refused 'cell is the index of a code cell, or the id of a cell you accepted'
findings.cause: the accept route was never relayed; a card showing {accepted: true} alone would have the person accept code they never saw
findings.fix: POST .../notebook/cells/{id}/answer relayed only as {accepted: bool}, after DCLab Code reads the cell from DCLab and shows its request, note and whole code; missing, answered or over 6,000 characters: never asked
findings.test: dclab-code tests/server.test.js (the card shows the code; three cells never asked), units (only {accepted: bool})

findings.scenario: accept instead of accepted, cell_id instead of cell, '500 rows' inside a description (the design made 5,000)
findings.cause: those routes take any JSON object; the agent sees only their docstrings
findings.fix: the docstrings name their body fields first (notebook run/write/answer, synthetic design and create)
findings.test: rerun s_8304a18907f1: the design kept 500 rows, the run sent {cell}

findings.defect: the notebook's run was asked as a holdout read
findings.scenario: s_8304a18907f1: the card said it reads the holdout
findings.cause: the holdout pattern /run$ matched /notebook/run; the kernel has the training rows only
findings.fix: the pattern names the project's run-all only
findings.test: units: notebook run is a decision, build/run, programme/run and stages/final/run stay holdout

findings.defect: a saved config pinned the code's default guards
findings.scenario: adding a project wrote every default guard to config.json; a corrected default never took effect; pushing to a loaded config changed the module's own HOLDOUT_CALLS
findings.cause: saveConfig wrote the merged config; defaultConfig handed out module arrays
findings.fix: only the person's own guards are saved (ownGuards), a fresh home too; the defaults are copies
findings.test: units: saving keeps only the person's own guards

findings.defect: starting a team was asked as a holdout read
findings.scenario: both teams pause for the person before their build or holdout
findings.fix: only the person's approve: true is asked as one (whenBody)

findings.defect: the solution team's report was always empty on a project of one problem
findings.cause: the report step read a summary the final record does not have, and kept only its length
findings.fix: it reports studio.solution_report.latest (every number traced, built once per set of records) and the walk's answer carries it
findings.test: R&D tests/test_orchestra_solution.py (walked again on a finished project, the report names roc_auc; holdout_uses stays 1)

findings.defect: a chat could not start the understanding team
findings.cause: its route was not on the chat's write list
findings.fix: added; its answers, map confirmation and build approval stay the person's (relayed)

findings.defect: no way to save the solution from the chat
findings.scenario: s_bb85024f2fdf: 'Save the solution first' on a team-built project
findings.cause: saving is the person's PUT, and the relay took POSTs only
findings.fix: PUT .../solution relayed, the whole solution on the card (up to 6,000 characters)
findings.test: units: PUT only for the solution, every kept-out column on the card

findings.defect: a long write reached the chat as 'The operation timed out'
findings.scenario: s_57386a4805dd: the team's start ran four stages inside the request
findings.cause: the SDK's MCP tool-call limit; R&D's bridge waited for the whole route
findings.fix: R&D's bridge runs each request as its own task and, for a write, answers after 100 s 'still working, never send it again, follow it with GET ...'; DCLab Code's limit for DCLab's server is 300 s
findings.test: R&D LongWriteTests; dclab-code units (the timeout above R&D's longest wait)

findings.defect: a solution team's drop answer reads the holdout, but its card no longer said so
findings.scenario: a programme with a part that cannot run: the person approves the holdout, the part blocks it, the team asks 'drop it?'; {answer: ...} was a plain decision card, and on Allow compose saw approved_for == audited and ran the programme, reading the holdout
findings.cause: narrowing the team's holdout pattern to approve: true missed the answer that resumes after an approval
findings.fix: a project team's answer is asked as a holdout read too (whenBodyHas), and its card says it may go on to read it
findings.test: dclab-code units (a drop answer is holdout); server test (the card says so)

findings.defect: a relayed team approval never showed what it approved
findings.scenario: the agent draws a map (agent work), starts the walk, the walk pauses on the map's confirmation; the card showed only {approve: true}, and Allow confirmed a map the person never saw (the same for overriding the critic's concerns)
findings.cause: only the cell answer read its content before the card
findings.fix: a team's answer or approval reads GET /api/{drafts|projects}/{id}/team through the person's channel and puts the pause's kind, gate, question and whole summary on the card; no pause open, or a summary over 6,000 characters: never asked; a holdout read said only when the answer can go on to one
findings.test: dclab-code server test: the map's parts on the card, the holdout gate and the drop answer said as holdout reads, nothing asked or sent with no pause

findings.defect: a cell's code lost its lines and indentation on the card
findings.scenario: 'if False:\n    x = 1\nopen(p).read()' and the same with open(p) indented looked identical; an accepted cell runs on the host
findings.fix: pre-wrap (and a scroll for long text)
findings.test: dclab-code page test in Chromium: two cells differing only in indentation look different

findings.defect: small: the cut team report pointed to another document; sync-check passed silently when R&D's writes could not be listed whole
findings.scenario: GET .../export/report serves a different report; more than 100 POST routes made writeOperations return null
findings.cause: wrong route name; a null treated as nothing to check
findings.fix: the link names /export/solution-report; sync-check reports 'not checked' as a change

measurements.name: tests
measurements.result: dclab-code 103 of 103 (units, server, Chromium page tests); R&D test_chat_agents, test_orchestra_solution, test_agents_validator, and the orchestra and harness files (111)

outcome: Every R&D agent that serves the product is reached from the chat or stays the person's for a stated reason; the person's decisions reach DCLab as their own clicks, each card showing exactly what is sent.
lessons: Check each agent end to end with its model on: the solution team's empty report hid behind a passing test that never read the report.
When a route takes any JSON object, its description must name the fields, or the agent guesses.
A long job behind a tool call must answer before the caller's limit and say how to follow it, or the caller repeats it.
When a pattern of asks is narrowed to be honest, list every way the guarded thing can still happen before removing a case: the drop answer resumed straight into the holdout.
risks: the relay's ask card is text: a long solution or cell is shown whole but may not be read whole
CALL_WAIT_S and the SDK limit are tuned by hand; a slower machine may need more
a config.json written before this keeps the old, broader holdout entry as the person's own: more asking, never less
